body:
What's the status on this? This seems to be the perfect solution to something I have yet to find a clean alternative for, and plugins can't really hook into the inner workings of the theming system.

I'd be glad to help out or pick this up if necessary, but I'm moreso just curious to know what thoughts are on this? Theming is definitely missing a lot of love compared to other parts of Godot, so this would be really nice to see
It should be in a fully working state. It's waiting on reviews and feedback, particularly on if this approach is even ok from the maintainers

Just tested it. Seems to work great on my end 👍

Would be nice to be able to somehow handle the properties individually, but this already accomplishes everything I've really needed. Might just use this fork for the time being, lol

Yeah I had it working with individual properties at some point, but it really bloated the inspector, and caused long freezes when first inspecting an element. It would probably need a custom editor plugin to make that feel usable

I'm surprised there's been no discussion on this yet - revisiting this PR because I'm currently working on a plugin that also has the functionality to animate styleboxes. Even though the scope of the plugin has grown far past "animating styleboxes", and I now have mostly everything that I've been needing, it'd still be nice to have something like this in the base engine. 

Don't know if I'm allowed to show any details regarding the plugin here since I don't want to come off as "advertising", but I've been fixing a lot of shortcomings I've encountered when it comes to stylebox theming in Godot; and it'd be cool to see some discussion on the system - either here or perhaps linked somewhere else 🤔

@cruglet It definitely sounds interesting. Is it your gdss repo? I didn't see a readme, so not sure how it works, but I'd be interested to hear how you approached it and if there's a better way than this PR

@dugramen Yeah, it is that repo. And I've updated it to include a readme with some info on how it works.

However, my approach is probably not the most ideal either way because it hooks into the base theming system by overriding styleboxes into one shared resource per-node. It *is* opt-in and the intention of the plugin is not to be handled with the builtin theme editor, but this pr would definitely be the much safer and consistent approach with the current theming system, granted its implementation is fine internally.

@dugramen Could you look into [rebasing this PR](https://contributing.godotengine.org/en/latest/pull_requests/creating_pull_requests.html#the-interactive-rebase) to fix merge conflicts? While 4.7 is now in feature freeze, I'd like to review this for the 4.8 cycle.

Rebased it. 

Though coming back to it, I'm not a fan of one aspect of it. Currently animation info, like duration ease & transition, are inside each StyleBox. But they can affect theme colors too, and require repetition. It might be better to move it into a separate theme data type for animation info
Oops I think "Unset" is from a previous version, I had tried to make the "normal" stylebox act like the default and the others could optionally inherit from it, but it wasn't reliable

I don't know if this is within the scope of this PR, but it would be very useful to have offset properties in the stylebox (such as translate and scale) to create more possibilities and allow tweaks that would require code Edit: thinking twice, this might be better off as an standalone PR to separate concerns, since it would be useful without transitions too. I'll create a proposal later Edit: I create the proposal: https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/15226

Tested it, think this feels really polished. Had a lot of fun making little buttons with this, you can get some way towards the effect @paulovbettio mentioned by fiddling with margins. Ran into one small bug (don't know if this is specific to this pr honestly): when you change the content margin on a hover or pressed state, the size of the stylebox sometimes isn't updated. It does update briefly when you change the color. Anyway, great work!
Sorry I didn't realize I never finished making all the suggested changes. I'll try to get this done tomorrow

I pushed the changes, and removed custom ID, as its confusing and would be better just to have a flag on TabBar for a single sliding tab animation (didn't add that yet though, not sure if it should be in this pr)
Rebased and fixed conflicts

Ah that seems right. Thanks for investigating, I'll try to update it today

this is an awesome PR! Hope it gets merged soon.

Was just messing around with it a bit, I think one thing that I'm not sure is possible with this system is different animations based on states to and from. E.g. It feels nice to have a snappy animation when a button is hovered (0.0s) but then to have a slow animation when the button is released, however, because the mouse will be over the button when it's released, it will use the timing for the hovered state, not the normal state.

I'm not sure what the best solution is for this though, one thought I had was each state could have a "state entry" and "state exit" time, which you could then just add together? 

And then maybe for clarity the current "Exiting" could be renamed to "Freeing" or something...?

Anyway not necessary features but would be a useful addition IMO.
I don't think "freeing" is appropriate, in what way is it freeing the stylebox?

My understanding was that the current exit animation plays when it transitions to not having a stylebox any more, so that's what I meant by freeing. But I also agree freeing is probably not a clear name in this context, maybe it's fine as is.
From my reading of the documentation that's not how it is, it's when it has no animation frames left

Yeah no worries, that part can probably stay as is anyway.

My main point was just that it would be useful to have an entry and exit state animation config (but then the side effect is it might be confusing to the user as there's already an exit animation but for a different purpose).
